title: Arthur Briggs gets him a job at the Ostend casino
summary: Back in Paris with no summer work, trumpeter Arthur Briggs found him a job at the Ostend/Knokke casino, where he sang English songs with Red de Broy's group.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: Yeah, July '39. I got back, things looked bad. We didn't have no summer gig and it was hot,

and when it's hot in Paris, you really hot, man.
Things was very bad, so, a fellow named Briggs,
Arthur Briggs, a trumpet player, he was a great trumpet
player.

He, Arthur Briggs was a New Yorker
but I think originally he was from there.--I mean West Indian--Caribbean person.
So, all right, Briggs got a job for me to entertain at a place called The Paragola--Oostende-- East end.
Right across from Dover. You can see the boat coming in over there at 5:00 o'clock every day.
Englishmen would come to Oostende (phonetic) for their vacations, you see. / The working class people. Now, this place that we were playing in, it was for the rich people, the casino, they had a symphony orchestra and they had us there.
They had a symphony orchestra all the time. That was a big casino. They used to call it the Knokke....., the Casino de Knokke.
So, I got that job to go to Austern. We stayed there and then it got rougher and rougher. And people start to making it home, and where we're coming from but I keep seeing lot of other new people coming in. They didn't seem to be worried at all.
So, all right, I -- I'm playing, and they had a boy by the name of Red DuBoy. (phonetic). He was a saxophone
Red DuBroy. He was from Holland.
No, Red -- it was De Broy, because see, the Dutch people have names like that.

So, he was a nice saxophone player and he had a little girl sing with him called Jope van Deiffe- she was nice, sang nice, pretty little girl too, and then we had a piano player named Gaston. And then the drums, so we had, so I would sing English songs and the people, in unison, everybody would sing and everybody was happy.
So, we were doing good and the money was beautiful. It was lovely.
So, all right. We were getting ready to close August 15, I mean, September 15, they closed and people go to the city.
